correctness.rationale: Roulleau's full text gives exactly six \((-2)\)-curves, the three relations \(A_1+A_4=A_2+A_5=A_3+A_6=2D\), the deck action \(A_j\mapsto A_{j+3}\), and \(\operatorname{Aut}(X)\cong C_2\). Any smooth six-tangent conic has even branch divisor on \(\mathbb P^1\), hence splits upstairs into a deck-exchanged pair of smooth rational curves, necessarily among those six. The exact presentation fiber follows from UFD factorization in \(\mathbb C[x,y,z]\): if \((f'-f)(f'+f)=(c-1)q_1q_2q_3\) with \(c\ne1\), a nonzero degree-three factor would have to be a product of degree-two irreducibles, impossible. Projective branch stabilizers lift to the double cover, forcing triviality because the only K3 automorphisms are identity and deck involution.

value.rationale: The invariant is attached to the natural parameterization used to build the entire \(S_1\) moduli family. The source's dimension count removes obvious continuous rescalings but does not identify the fiber. Proving that the three splitting conics are complete, that the square presentation is unique modulo the visible action, and that the branch sextic has no projective isotropy gives an exact moduli-level rigidity statement rather than a recomputation of a tabulated invariant.
